macro.headline: Bull regime intact but tech drag and geopolitical shock cap upside.
macro.story:
The tape is genuinely split. SPY sits at 747.71, +0.9% on the week and 8.4% above its 200-day, with MACD constructive and RSI at 55 — a bull regime by every structural measure. But underneath, QQQ is down 2.0% on the week and 4.1% on the month, below its 50-day and with a clearly negative MACD histogram, while the Dow is running hot (RSI 68.9) as capital rotates into cyclicals and defensives. VIX popped 8.7% in a day to 17.54 (+6.6% over 5d), 10-year yields pushed to 4.53%, DXY holds a firm uptrend, and both gold and silver are in confirmed downtrends — the classic dollar-strength commodity headwind is live. WTI ripped +4.6% on the day to $73.66, decoupling from the broader commodity weakness.

The prevailing sentiment across the tracked conversation leans firmly bearish and attributes the wobble to two threads. First, geopolitics: the dominant view is that Trump's declaration that the Iran ceasefire is 'over' — plus threats to cut trade with Spain — is what jolted crude higher and futures lower, with tracked chart reads specifically flagging Brent's spike toward $79 as the proximate catalyst. This aligns cleanly with the oil price data. Second, and more important for equity direction, the tracked conversation is bearish on the AI/semi complex: names like AMD, GOOGL, AAOI, COHR and QQQ dominate the negative posts, framed around 'AI capex' and 'Meta Compute' concerns, with one tracked read explicitly noting 'Nasdaq down 1.65%, semis and AI names getting hit hard.' This narrative is consistent with the sector data — Technology and the Nasdaq 100 are the only two sectors ranked BEARISH — so sentiment and price are singing the same song here. The lone bullish voice is idiosyncratic (CXW) and does not offset the broader lean.

The rotation implication is clear and validated by the sector engine: Healthcare, Consumer Staples, Industrials and Utilities are HOT with bullish MACDs, Financials is qualifying on a very hot RSI (74.4), and Tech is out. Six of eleven GICS sectors sit above their 50-day. The rotation radar highlights Health Information Services, Diagnostics & Research, Credit Services, Travel Services and Advertising Agencies as validated Early-Runway industries — all still early in their hot spells with above-median cross-sectional RS. That is where the confirmed tailwind lives today.

Forward watch: whether the Iran headline escalates further (a second leg higher in crude and VIX would push macro confidence to LOW), whether QQQ can reclaim its 50-day (a rejection there confirms the leadership handoff to cyclicals/defensives), and whether Financials' 74 RSI cools without breaking trend. VIX at 17.5 is elevated but not stressed — the washout signal is not engaged.
